declared.title: Eyewitness Memory Distortion Following Co-Witness Discussion: A Replication of Garry, French, Kinzett, and Mori (2008) in Ten Countries
declared.venue: Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « multi-lab registered replication misinformation memory eyewitness » (preprint), then Crossref search « co-witness discussion memory conformity MORI technique replication countries » (2026-11-23)

population: 486 university students tested in pairs in 10 countries (Brazil, Canada, Colombia, India, Japan, Malaysia, Poland, Portugal, Turkey, UK)

findings.text: In each of the 10 countries, after discussing a film with a partner who had seen a different version, people often reported details they never saw but their partner had mentioned

support.sentence: Each of the 10 samples replicated the Garry et al. finding: Participants often reported on the final test a non-witnessed answer that their co-witness had stated during the collaboration phase.

findings.text: Such errors were especially likely when the person had not disputed the partner's account during the discussion

support.sentence: Such co-witness suggestibility errors were especially likely when the witness had not disputed the co-witness's report during the collaboration phase.

findings.text: The authors conclude the co-witness effect replicates and generalizes across countries

support.sentence: The results demonstrate the replicability and generalizability of the co-witness suggestibility effect.

findings.text: About 8 in 10 of the details a partner had stated (and the person had not seen) were later picked the partner's way on a two-choice test: the authors' translation of the pooled effect

support.sentence: These two effect sizes translate to 80.2% (and 81.5%) of the items in which the participant was exposed to misleading information from the co-witness being answered incorrectly.
support.readBy: memory-rewritten reviser, 2026-11-26: accepted manuscript (WRAP 108300), Results, meta-analysis paragraph

findings.text: When the person had stated their own version too (a disputed detail), only 1 case in 58 was later reported the partner's way: an unplanned analysis

support.sentence: In contrast, across the 58 cases of disputed co-witness answers, only in one case (1.8%) did the witness err on the final test by reporting the co-witness's detail.
support.readBy: memory-rewritten reviser, 2026-11-26: accepted manuscript (WRAP 108300), Results, disputed vs non-disputed answers

limits: half preregistered, late: the 2nd wave (5 samples) was set out on OSF in advance, but its formal registration was completed after collection (July 2018)
a lab film, peripheral details (a picture on a wall, a cap's colour), about 1.6 per person, and a two-choice test the same day: not a memory of one's own life
about 415 of 486 analysed (people exposed to no partner detail were left out); the effect ranged from 34% (Colombia) to 64% (Japan)
the authors link country differences to how often pairs disputed, and note they do not fit a larger effect in collectivist cultures
Turkey and Malaysia (Chinese-Malaysian students) are in the sample, no Arab country: not counted as MENA
